newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: China defence chief not changing Asia travel plans.
newsitem.headline: China defence chief not changing Asia travel plans.

text.p: China's defence chief would not cut short his visit to the Philippines and will go on to Indonesia on Thursday, a Chinese diplomat said on Tuesday.

"He will not change his programme. He will stay here until the 20th," a Chinese embassy political officer said when asked if Defence Minister Chi Haotian was changing his schedule in Manila following reports that paramount leader Deng Xiaoping's health was failing.

The officer said Chi was sticking to the rest of his Philippine itinerary which includes a tour on Tuesday of the World War Two island fortress of Corregidor, on the mouth of Manila Bay, and a call on President Fidel Ramos on Wednesday.
When asked if the embassy had heard any word about Deng's condition, the embassy officer said: "I don't know ... we don't have any report." He declined to be named.
Chi, who arrived on the weekend, called for increased cooperation between the Chinese and Philippine armed forces in talks on Monday with his Filipino counterpart, Renato de Villa.

In Beijing, the Chinese State Council, or cabinet, was silent on Tuesday on Deng's health after Communist Party chief Jiang Zemin and other leaders cut short out-of-town trips to visit the ailing patriarch.
The State Council, or cabinet, declined to make immediate comment on the rumours that the health of Deng, 92, had deteriorated recently or that he had suffered a stroke.
